answer: Every autonomous identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to access the network. A verifier checks the ledger for unique payments to ensure singular registration, acting like a sun-drenched dune to expose any duplicate agents. An honest entity pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens. Each identity must hold a specific 5GB umber-coded shard of validated historical data. Any reuse triggers a permanent slash of the burned assets, with evidence found along the ridge of the audit trail.
